content_voiceover: This flowchart operationalizes CRS management by grade. Grades two through four all trigger an ICU notification, and every grade gets blood cultures, an infectious workup, prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics, and supportive symptom management like antipyretics and fluid resuscitation. Starting at grade two, and continuing through grades three and four, you initiate specific CRS-directed therapy, which for higher grades means completing IV tocilizumab at eight milligrams per kilogram, capped at eight hundred milligrams, before transferring the patient to the ICU. If grade two worsens, add dexamethasone ten milligrams every six hours for one to three days; if it progresses further, escalate to dexamethasone twenty milligrams every six hours for three days with a taper over three to seven days. If there's no improvement twelve hours after the first tocilizumab dose, repeat tocilizumab at the same weight-based dose. For grade one with no improvement after three days and no alternative diagnosis, consider tocilizumab as well, though it's a lower urgency pathway. If symptoms persist despite dexamethasone and repeat tocilizumab, the algorithm escalates to high-dose methylprednisolone: one thousand milligrams daily for three days, then tapering through two hundred fifty milligrams twice daily, one twenty-five twice daily, and sixty twice daily, each step for two days. And critically, repeat tocilizumab dosing should only be considered if the patient has not developed ICANS, since IL-6 blockade can theoretically worsen neurotoxicity.
keypoints: Grade 2-4 CRS triggers ICU notification; all grades get cultures, prophylactic antibiotics, supportive care
Tocilizumab 8mg/kg (max 800mg) IV completed before ICU transfer for higher grades
Escalating dexamethasone: 10mg every 6h, then 20mg every 6h with taper if worsening
No improvement 12h after tocilizumab, repeat the tocilizumab dose
Refractory disease escalates to high-dose methylprednisolone taper; repeat tocilizumab only if no ICANS present
keypoint_voiceover: ICU notification kicks in at grade two and up, alongside cultures and prophylactic antibiotics for every grade. Tocilizumab at eight milligrams per kilogram is the first specific therapy, escalating dexamethasone if it worsens, and repeating tocilizumab if there's no improvement at twelve hours. Refractory cases move to high-dose methylprednisolone with a taper. Remember, repeat tocilizumab is only appropriate if the patient hasn't developed ICANS.
